tasks.name: m5-suggestion-apply
tasks.scopedGoal:
Land M5 suggestion-apply end-to-end against the M4 deliverable branch (`orch/pr-cockpit/m4-merge-multiaccount`). Two paths per PLAN.md §5.4 + §8 + §12 M5 + AUTONOMY_BRIEF.md §M5:

* **Single-suggestion apply** via the GitHub mutation (or REST equivalent) when available — no local worktree required.
* **Batched-suggestion apply** gated on a CLEAN local worktree mapped to the PR; the engine writes the suggestions into the working tree, commits on the PR's head branch with a Co-authored-by attribution to each suggestion's author, and pushes through `git2` (the worktree-write side from PLAN.md §8). The whole flow is no-optimism (PLAN.md §3.2): confirm + dirty-state snapshot + commit + push + server confirms + reconcile.

The M3 worktree-read module already discovers worktrees and maps them to PRs with confidence; this task is the FIRST worktree-WRITE work in the repo, so be deliberate about the safety net (PLAN.md §8: 'Cleanup blocked on user-managed worktrees; app-created cleanup requires confirmation + dirty-state snapshot. Never delete uncommitted work.'). Apply the same standard to writes.

### Deliverables

1) **Backend (Rust, `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/`)**

   a) **Single-suggestion-apply via GitHub** — investigate GraphQL `applySuggestion` / REST `/pulls/{n}/comments/{comment_id}/replies` + suggestion commit endpoints. As of 2026-05-18 the public-facing path that github.com itself uses for a single suggestion is `POST /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/reviews` with an event `COMMENT` and an inline body that turns into a commit — the canonical mechanism is documented under GitHub's REST 'Apply suggested change' (or octokit equivalent). Implement whichever path is currently working: try the `git commit-changes` REST endpoint `PUT /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/comments/{comment_id}` with the suggestion JSON; if that 404s or returns 'not implemented', fall back to fetching the file, applying the suggestion in-memory, and committing via REST `PUT /repos/{o}/{r}/contents/{path}`. Document the chosen path in DECISIONS.md verbatim with the request/response shape. Tests use wiremock to stub the chosen endpoint.

   b) **MutationKind additions** in `mutations::MutationKind` (kinds 35 + 36 after the existing 34):
      * `ApplySuggestion` — input: `{ review_comment_id, expected_head_sha }`. OptimismLevel::None. apply() calls the chosen GitHub endpoint. reconcile() refetches the PR detail + diff + thread state. On 409 (head moved), emit `MutationEvent::HardConflict` with a structured 'Head branch advanced — suggestion no longer applies, please re-comment' message.
      * `ApplySuggestionBatch` — input: `{ pr_id, suggestion_ids: Vec<String>, expected_head_sha, worktree_path }`. OptimismLevel::None. apply() runs the local worktree-write flow (described in 1c below). reconcile() refetches PR + thread state on success.

   c) **Worktree-write module** `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/worktree/write.rs`:
      * `pub struct WorktreeWriteRequest { pub pr_id: String, pub worktree_path: PathBuf, pub expected_branch: String, pub expected_head_sha: String, pub suggestions: Vec<SuggestionPatch>, pub author: AuthorIdentity, pub message: String }`.
      * `pub struct SuggestionPatch { pub path: PathBuf, pub start_line: u32, pub end_line: u32, pub side: DiffSide, pub replacement: String, pub original_commit_sha: String, pub suggestion_author_login: String }` — coordinates match GitHub's `line`/`side`/`start_line`/`start_side` per PLAN.md §6.
      * `pub struct WorktreeWriteOutcome { pub head_sha_before: String, pub head_sha_after: String, pub commit_sha: String, pub pushed: bool, pub dirty_snapshot: Option<PathBuf>, pub coauthors: Vec<String> }`.
      * `pub trait WorktreeWriter { fn run(&self, req: WorktreeWriteRequest) -> Result<WorktreeWriteOutcome, WorktreeWriteError>; }` with the concrete `Git2WorktreeWriter` implementation using `git2`:
         1. Open the repo at `worktree_path` via `git2::Repository::open`.
         2. Assert the active branch matches `expected_branch` AND `HEAD == expected_head_sha`. Otherwise return `BranchMismatch` / `HeadMismatch`.
         3. Assert the worktree is clean: `repo.statuses(None)` returns an empty set. If dirty, take a `git stash push --include-untracked` snapshot first ONLY if the user explicitly opted in (controlled by the request flag `force_with_stash: bool`, default false); otherwise return `WorktreeDirty { snapshot_command_hint }`. NEVER silently stash.
         4. For each `SuggestionPatch`, read the file, splice in the replacement at `[start_line..=end_line]` (inclusive, 1-indexed, side-aware), and write back. Suggestions whose `original_commit_sha` doesn't equal `expected_head_sha` and the corresponding lines in the file don't match the expected `original` content are rejected with `SuggestionConflict` (we never blindly overwrite).
         5. Stage all modified files. Build a commit message: a one-line summary + a per-suggestion `Co-authored-by: <login> <login@users.noreply.github.com>` trailer for every distinct suggestion author. Commit via `git2::Repository::commit` with the active user as committer + author.
         6. Push via `git2::PushOptions` with the auth callback wired to the keychain-stored token for the PR's account (the same plumbing the existing API client uses). Refuse to push if the remote head has advanced (require `--force-with-lease` semantics; assert by listing the remote ref first via the same client and bailing on mismatch). On rejection, return `PushRejected { remote_head }`.
         7. Emit per-step Tauri events `worktree_write:<pr_id>:<step>` (`opened`, `assertions_ok`, `patched`, `committed`, `pushed`) so the UI shows a live progress bar.
      * Errors: a single `WorktreeWriteError` enum capturing every failure mode above. Implementing `Display + Error` + `serde::Serialize + specta::Type` so the UI can render structured messages.
      * Tests under `apps/desktop/src-tauri/tests/worktree_write.rs`:
         - Happy-path: temp `git init` repo, two file fixtures, apply a batch of three suggestions, assert the resulting commit's tree hash + author + co-author trailers + push (use a bare local remote as the push target).
         - WorktreeDirty: same setup but `echo dirty > file`; assert the writer returns `WorktreeDirty` without modifying anything.
         - BranchMismatch: HEAD on a different branch; assert `BranchMismatch`.
         - HeadMismatch: HEAD advanced from `expected_head_sha`; assert `HeadMismatch`.
         - SuggestionConflict: the file's lines at the patch range don't match the suggestion's original; assert `SuggestionConflict` + no file mutation.
         - PushRejected: remote head advanced between commit and push; assert `PushRejected` + the local commit is rolled back via `git reset --hard <head_sha_before>`.
         - Force-with-stash opt-in: `force_with_stash: true` with dirty worktree → assert stash created + applied back after the write completes.

   d) **Suggestion-block detection in markdown** — extend the existing comrak pipeline (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/render/`) to detect ` ```suggestion ... ``` ` fenced code blocks AND emit a `SuggestionBlock { id, body, start_line, end_line, side, comment_id, original_commit_sha, suggestion_author_login }` per detected block. Persist them to a new `suggestion_blocks` read-model view backed by `review_comments` (the block text is in the comment body — no new table needed; derive at read time). The view exposes one row per suggestion block per review comment. Add an IPC `list_suggestion_blocks(pr_id) -> Vec<SuggestionBlockView>` so the UI can render a 'Suggested changes' palette on the PR.

   e) **Dispatch wiring** in `mutations::dispatch::dispatch_for_kind`: route `ApplySuggestion` → 1a handler; route `ApplySuggestionBatch` → the worktree-write flow.

2) **Frontend (Svelte 5, Primer CSS, `apps/desktop/src/`)**

   a) Extend `Composer.svelte` and the timeline review-comment renderer to surface 'Apply suggestion' as a Primer-styled button on every detected suggestion block. Single-click runs the `ApplySuggestion` mutation through the existing `NoOptimismButton` flow (confirm → spinner → server confirms → reconcile). The button is disabled when the comment is outdated (uses the existing `isOutdated` field) with a tooltip explaining why.

   b) New component `apps/desktop/src/lib/components/suggestions/SuggestionBatchModal.svelte`:
      * Triggered from a 'Apply N suggestions' button surfaced in the PR detail right-rail when the PR has 2+ open suggestion blocks. The modal lists each suggestion as a checkbox row with the file + line range + a small inline preview of the replacement.
      * Below the list, a 'Worktree' panel: shows the mapped worktree path (from M3 worktree mapping) with confidence + the current dirty status. If no worktree is mapped, the modal asks the user to map one first (link to settings).
      * If the worktree is dirty, the modal blocks submission and shows a clear 'Worktree is dirty — commit or stash your changes first, or check `Force with stash` (advanced)' affordance.
      * Submit runs the `ApplySuggestionBatch` mutation through the `NoOptimismButton` flow with a progress bar driven by the `worktree_write:*` Tauri events (renders the five steps live).
      * On success, shows the new HEAD sha + commit URL + a green 'Pushed' chip. On failure, surfaces the structured `WorktreeWriteError` with a per-error remediation hint.

   c) **PR detail page integration**: above the timeline, when the PR has 2+ open suggestion blocks, render a sticky Primer banner 'N pending suggestions — Apply N' that opens the SuggestionBatchModal. Keyboard: `g s` opens the modal (registered in the existing layout-level keymap; the command palette task will wire it into the palette later).

3) **DB migrations** — `apps/desktop/src-tauri/migrations/0013_suggestion_apply.sql` adds a `suggestion_applies` audit table: `(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, account_id TEXT NOT NULL, pr_id TEXT NOT NULL, mutation_id TEXT NOT NULL, mode TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (mode IN ('single', 'batch')), commit_sha TEXT, head_sha_before TEXT, head_sha_after TEXT, suggestion_comment_ids TEXT NOT NULL, applied_at INTEGER NOT NULL, outcome TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (outcome IN ('applied', 'conflict', 'aborted', 'rejected')), error_kind TEXT)`. Used by the audit log surfaced in the SyncErrorsTray for failed batches. Provide `0013_suggestion_apply.down.sql`.

4) **Playwright spec** `apps/desktop/playwright/m5-suggestion-apply.spec.ts`:
   * Single-suggestion path: PR fixture with a suggestion block on review comment id `r1`. Click 'Apply suggestion' → NoOptimismButton confirm modal → mocked IPC `submit_mutation('apply_suggestion', …)` fires → server confirms via mocked reconcile → the suggestion-block UI shows 'Applied'. Screenshot to `artifacts/m5-suggestion-apply/single.png`.
   * Batched path with clean worktree: PR fixture with 3 suggestion blocks + a mapped clean worktree fixture (use the M3 worktree mapping fixture machinery). Open the batch modal → check 2 of 3 → confirm → assert the per-step progress events render → final 'Pushed' chip + new HEAD chip. Screenshot stream to `artifacts/m5-suggestion-apply/batch/01..05.png` for each step.
   * Batched path with dirty worktree: same as above but the fixture worktree is dirty → assert the modal blocks submission and renders the 'Worktree is dirty' message. Screenshot to `artifacts/m5-suggestion-apply/dirty-blocked.png`.
   * Force-with-stash opt-in: enable the advanced checkbox → submit → assert the stash + apply-batch + stash-pop sequence runs.
   * Head-mismatch conflict: fixture where `expected_head_sha` doesn't match the mocked HEAD → assert `HeadMismatch` error renders with the structured remediation hint.

5) **DECISIONS.md** — dated M5 entry covering: (a) the GitHub single-suggestion endpoint chosen + verbatim request/response shape; (b) the worktree-write safety contract (clean-worktree required, force-with-stash opt-in, force-with-lease push semantics, dirty snapshot in `dirty_snapshot` path); (c) the suggestion-block detection algorithm + how the read-model derives suggestion rows from review_comments; (d) the per-suggestion-author Co-authored-by trailer format; (e) the `worktree_write:*` event schema + the five step names.

### Guardrails
- Do NOT touch the check-annotations surface, the saved-replies palette, the paste-image-upload flow, or the command-palette UI — those are owned by sibling tasks.
- The renderer never opens SQLite, never shells out to git, never calls GitHub directly — only IPC.
- Tokens stay in the keychain across worktree pushes (the git2 push callback reads the existing keychain-stored token); no token bytes in any log line, IPC payload, `suggestion_applies` row, or committed artifact.
- All M4 tests must remain green.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm svelte-check`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test` green at handoff. Playwright `m5-suggestion-apply.spec.ts` under xvfb.
- Commit + push to the cloud-agent branch. No PR, no rename, no rebase.
acceptance: `ApplySuggestion` + `ApplySuggestionBatch` MutationKind variants exist, are dispatched, and are OptimismLevel::None.

`worktree::write::Git2WorktreeWriter` performs the open → assert-branch → assert-head → assert-clean → patch-files → commit → push flow with per-step Tauri events and an enumerated `WorktreeWriteError`.
Worktree-write safety: dirty worktree blocks submission; `force_with_stash` opt-in stash-and-restore works; head/branch mismatches return structured errors; push uses force-with-lease semantics.
Suggestion-block detection emits structured `SuggestionBlock` rows from review_comments; the `list_suggestion_blocks` IPC + `0013_suggestion_apply.sql` audit table are in place.

Frontend: per-suggestion 'Apply suggestion' button on review comments; SuggestionBatchModal lists suggestions, surfaces worktree state, runs through NoOptimismButton with live progress; sticky banner appears on PRs with 2+ suggestions.
Playwright `m5-suggestion-apply.spec.ts` covers single + batched-clean + batched-dirty-blocked + force-with-stash + head-mismatch with recorded artifacts under `artifacts/m5-suggestion-apply/`.
All gates green at handoff: cargo fmt/clippy/test, pnpm typecheck/svelte-check/lint/test, all prior M3/M4 Playwright specs + the new m5-suggestion-apply spec under xvfb.
DECISIONS.md updated with the single-suggestion endpoint choice, worktree-write safety contract, suggestion-block detection algorithm, Co-authored-by format, and `worktree_write:*` event schema.

tasks.name: m5-check-annotations
tasks.scopedGoal:
Land M5 check-annotations on the diff + failed-job log tail + rerun checks per AUTONOMY_BRIEF.md §M5 + PLAN.md §5.4 + §12 M5. The `check_annotations` table already exists from M1; this task makes it actually populated, rendered inline in the diff viewer at the right line, with a streaming failed-job log tail and rerun controls (single check-run and whole check-suite).

Before starting your own work, **merge the m5-suggestion-apply branch into your current branch**:
```bash
git fetch origin orch/m5-editor-power-worktree-write/m5-suggestion-apply
git merge --no-ff origin/orch/m5-editor-power-worktree-write/m5-suggestion-apply
```
Resolve conflicts (likely none — different surface area) and ensure all m5-suggestion-apply tests still pass before adding your changes. This avoids the M4 sibling-only star-topology pitfall flagged by the m4 verifier.

### Deliverables

1) **Backend (Rust, `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/`)**

   a) **Check-annotations sync** — new module `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/sync/check_annotations.rs`:
      * `pub async fn sync_check_annotations(account_id, repo, check_run_id) -> Result<Vec<CheckAnnotation>>` calls REST `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/check-runs/{check_run_id}/annotations` with pagination (per_page=100). Stores each annotation into `check_annotations` (idempotent upsert keyed by `(check_run_id, id)`).
      * Triggered from the existing PrDetail reconciliation loop when a check_run's `updated_at` advances OR when the run transitions from queued/in_progress to completed with non-zero failures. Background-task throttled per the per-account RateLimitBudgeter (M4) on the REST resource.
      * Persist a `check_annotation_aux` row mapping `(annotation_id) → (pr_id, account_id, anchor_line, anchor_side, anchor_path, anchor_signature_hash)` so the diff viewer can look up annotations by file + line in O(1).
      * Add migration `0014_check_annotations_aux.sql` adding the `check_annotation_aux` table + indexes on `(pr_id, anchor_path, anchor_line)` and `(check_run_id)`. Provide `.down.sql`.

   b) **Anchoring rules** — match the M3 review-thread anchoring: store GitHub's annotation `path` + `start_line` + `end_line` verbatim; derive `anchor_side` as `RIGHT` (annotations always anchor on the new revision). Never locally re-anchor across force-pushes; rely on the next sync to refresh against the new head_sha.

   c) **Failed-job log tail** — `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/api/check_logs.rs`:
      * `pub async fn stream_check_run_log(account_id, repo, check_run_id, tail_lines: usize) -> impl Stream<Item = LogChunk>`. Implementation: REST `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/actions/jobs/{job_id}/logs` (the API redirects to an Azure blob URL with a signed token; follow the redirect, stream the body in chunks of 8 KB, decode UTF-8 lossy, and yield each chunk through a Tauri channel). When `tail_lines` is set, buffer the last N lines client-side and emit them as a single 'tail' message (use a ring buffer to avoid loading the full log into memory; large logs can exceed 100 MB).
      * If the check run isn't a GitHub Actions job (e.g. external CI integrations), fall back to the `details_url` plus a 'View full log on GitHub' chip — do NOT attempt to scrape third-party CI consoles.
      * IPC: `start_check_log_stream(check_run_id, tail_lines) -> StreamHandle`. Emits `check_log:<check_run_id>:chunk` events. Backed by a Tauri `Channel<LogChunk>` so the stream cancels cleanly on UI unmount.
      * Tests: wiremock stub for the GitHub Actions jobs/logs redirect dance + the blob URL streaming; assert the tail buffer correctly yields the last N lines from a 10 KB fixture log.

   d) **Rerun checks** — extend the mutations engine with two new kinds (37 + 38):
      * `RerunCheckRun` — REST `POST /repos/{o}/{r}/check-runs/{check_run_id}/rerequest`. Per-account scoped; idempotency_key = `rerun:{check_run_id}:{head_sha}`. OptimismLevel::Cautious (shown as pending). Reconciles when the check transitions out of queued/in_progress.
      * `RerunCheckSuite` — GraphQL `rerunCheckSuite(input: { checkSuiteId })` — confirm the mutation name against the live GraphQL schema docs (alternative: REST `POST /repos/{o}/{r}/check-suites/{check_suite_id}/rerequest`). Document the choice in DECISIONS.md. OptimismLevel::Cautious.
      Both mutations refetch the PR's checks on success.

   e) **IPC** in `ipc/mod.rs`:
      * `list_check_annotations(pr_id) -> Vec<CheckAnnotationView>` — joins `check_annotations + check_annotation_aux + check_runs` and returns Specta-typed rows the diff viewer can render.
      * `list_check_annotations_for_file(pr_id, path) -> Vec<CheckAnnotationView>` — narrower, indexed for diff scroll perf.
      * `start_check_log_stream(check_run_id, tail_lines) -> StreamHandle` (per 1c above).
      * Regenerate `apps/desktop/src/lib/ipc/bindings.ts`.

   f) **Rust integration tests** under `apps/desktop/src-tauri/tests/`:
      * `check_annotations_sync.rs`: wiremock serves a 3-page annotations response; assert the engine upserts all rows into SQLite + the `check_annotation_aux` table.
      * `check_log_stream.rs`: wiremock serves the `/jobs/logs` redirect to a blob URL; assert the stream chunks + tail buffer behavior.
      * `rerun_check_run.rs`: wiremock stubs the rerequest endpoints; assert both `RerunCheckRun` + `RerunCheckSuite` mutations dispatch correctly with Cautious optimism.

2) **Frontend (Svelte 5, Primer CSS, `apps/desktop/src/`)**

   a) **Inline annotations in the diff viewer** — extend `DiffViewer.svelte`:
      * For each visible diff line, query `list_check_annotations_for_file(pr_id, path)` and render the matching annotations as inline Primer-styled gutter chips at the exact `(side, line)` coordinates. Severity styles: `failure` = red border-l + `octicon-x-circle`; `warning` = yellow border-l + `octicon-alert`; `notice` = blue border-l + `octicon-info`.
      * Click an annotation chip → expands an inline panel below the line with the full annotation `title` + `message` + `raw_details` (in a collapsible `<details>`), plus a 'View raw log' button that opens the failed-job log tail (see 2c).
      * Annotations dim when the PR's `head_sha` advances past the annotation's `check_run.head_sha` (indicating staleness); a tiny 'outdated' badge appears, matching the M3 review-thread outdated affordance.

   b) **Checks rail with rerun controls** — new component `apps/desktop/src/lib/components/checks/ChecksRail.svelte`:
      * Renders all `check_suites` + their `check_runs` for the active PR in a Primer-styled rail.
      * Each check_run has a 'Rerun' button (`octicon-sync`) for `RerunCheckRun`; each check_suite has a 'Rerun suite' button for `RerunCheckSuite`. Both wired through `submit_mutation` with the Cautious-optimism pending affordance from M2 (PendingAffordance.svelte).
      * Failed runs render an 'open log tail' icon (`octicon-terminal`) that opens the log-tail viewer (2c).
      * Replaces / extends whatever check rendering exists in the current PR detail page (locate it via `git grep CheckRun apps/desktop/src/`).

   c) **Failed-job log tail viewer** — new component `apps/desktop/src/lib/components/checks/CheckLogTail.svelte`:
      * Renders as a docked panel (right-rail or bottom-rail; pick the simpler layout and document in DECISIONS.md) with a monospaced log view bound to `start_check_log_stream(check_run_id, tail_lines=500)`.
      * Subscribes to `check_log:<check_run_id>:chunk` events; appends each chunk; preserves scroll position when the user scrolls up; auto-scrolls when pinned to bottom.
      * Shows a 'Stream live' toggle (when on, polls + appends; when off, freezes). Shows a 'Copy to clipboard' button.
      * On non-Actions checks (1c fallback), shows a 'View full log on GitHub' chip instead.

3) **Playwright spec** `apps/desktop/playwright/m5-check-annotations.spec.ts`:
   * Diff-viewer annotations: PR fixture with 3 check annotations (one failure, one warning, one notice) on `src/foo.ts` lines 12, 28, 47. Open the diff; assert each annotation renders at the correct line with the correct severity style. Click an annotation → assert the inline panel expands with the message + raw_details.
   * Failed-job log tail: open a failed check_run → assert the log-tail panel opens + receives chunked log events from the mocked stream + auto-scrolls.
   * Rerun check-run: click 'Rerun' on a check_run → assert `submit_mutation('rerun_check_run', …)` fires + the PendingAffordance shows 'queued'.
   * Rerun suite: click 'Rerun suite' on a check_suite → assert `submit_mutation('rerun_check_suite', …)` fires + all the suite's runs flip to pending.

Per-account because each account has its own github.com saved replies (PLAN.md §9: 'every viewer-dependent field is account-scoped'). Provide `.down.sql`.
   b) IPC commands in `ipc/mod.rs`:
      * `list_saved_replies(account_id) -> Vec<SavedReply>` — returns the per-account saved replies sorted by `sort_order ASC, name ASC`.
      * `create_saved_reply(account_id, name, body) -> SavedReply` — validates uniqueness on `(account_id, name)`, returns the inserted row.

      * `delete_saved_reply(id)`.

(The github.com saved-replies UI uses a graphql call too; verify either path works against the live API and pick whichever returns. If neither works, the import button is disabled with a 'GitHub does not expose saved replies via API; create them here' notice.)
      All Specta-typed; regenerate bindings.
   c) Tests: `saved_replies.rs` covers CRUD + per-account isolation (replies created under account A are not returned for account B) + reorder.

   a) **Settings page** — add a 'Saved replies' tab under `apps/desktop/src/routes/settings/` (or extend the existing settings page; locate via `git ls-files apps/desktop/src/routes/settings/`). A 'New saved reply' button opens a Primer modal with name + body textarea (using the same comrak preview pipeline the composer uses). Reorder via drag-handle (Primer styling). 'Import from GitHub' button (per 1b above, possibly disabled).

      * Add a 'Saved replies' button next to the existing Markdown/Preview tabs (`octicon-comment-discussion`). Click opens a small Primer-styled dropdown listing the active account's saved replies.

   d) **Composer.parity.test.ts** updated to assert that inserting a saved reply preserves the textarea + Preview parity (the inserted body renders identically through comrak in the Preview tab).

#### Paste-image-upload

3) **Backend (Rust)**:
   a) IPC command `upload_image_to_github_user_content(account_id, image_bytes, mime) -> ImageUploadResult { url, alt, content_hash, size_bytes }` in `ipc/mod.rs`. Implementation: github.com's image attachment uses the `https://uploads.github.com/{repo|user}/...` endpoint OR the older REST `POST https://uploads.github.com/repos/{o}/{r}/contents/.github/assets` flow. As of 2026-05-18, the canonical path is the `github.com/upload/assets/`-prefixed endpoint that the github.com UI itself uses (it's an internal but stable endpoint accessible with a regular user PAT). If both fail, fall back to `POST /markdown` rendering the image inline and store the raw bytes in the blob store with a content-addressed `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/assets/<sha>` URL — document the chosen path in DECISIONS.md.

tasks.scopedGoal:
Land M5 command palette + full keyboard layer per AUTONOMY_BRIEF.md §M5 + PLAN.md §10 + §12 M5. **PLAN.md §10 is a CI-enforced perf budget**: palette open < 75 ms, palette result < 150 ms. Both must be measured in `pnpm bench` and the bench must turn green at handoff.

Before starting your own work, **merge the upstream sibling branches into your current branch in order**:
```bash
git fetch origin orch/m5-editor-power-worktree-write/m5-suggestion-apply orch/m5-editor-power-worktree-write/m5-check-annotations orch/m5-editor-power-worktree-write/m5-saved-replies-paste-image

git merge --no-ff origin/orch/m5-editor-power-worktree-write/m5-check-annotations
git merge --no-ff origin/orch/m5-editor-power-worktree-write/m5-saved-replies-paste-image
```
Resolve conflicts and ensure all upstream tests still pass before adding your changes.

### Deliverables

1) **Frontend (Svelte 5, Primer CSS, `apps/desktop/src/`)**

   a) **Command registry** — `apps/desktop/src/lib/commands/registry.ts`:
      * `interface Command { id: string; title: string; section: string; keywords?: string[]; shortcut?: string; visibility?: (ctx: CommandContext) => boolean; run: (ctx: CommandContext) => Promise<void> | void; }`.
      * `interface CommandContext { activeAccountId: string; activeRoute: string; activePrId?: string; activeFilePath?: string; activeSuggestionId?: string; openModal: (id: string, props?: any) => void; navigate: (path: string) => void; submitMutation: (kind: string, payload: any) => Promise<void>; }`.
      * Registry shape: a single in-memory map keyed by command id with O(1) lookup + a sorted array for default ordering. Registration is static (commands declared in a single `commands.ts` file) PLUS dynamic (saved-replies registered at app-boot from the IPC `list_saved_replies`).
      * Static commands (minimum, matching the task brief): `palette.open` (Ctrl+K), `inbox.open` (g i), `pr.openByNumber` (g p), `account.switch` (Ctrl+Shift+A), `composer.open` (c), `composer.focus` (r), `suggestion.apply` (g s when on a PR with suggestions), `suggestion.applyBatch` (g S), `thread.resolve` (Ctrl+Shift+R when a thread is focused), `thread.unresolve` (Ctrl+Shift+U), `file.markViewed` (v when a file is focused in the diff), `file.unmarkViewed` (V), `pr.openInGithub` (Ctrl+Shift+O), `inbox.openInGithub` (g G), `pr.refresh` (Cmd+R / F5), `checks.rerunRun` (Ctrl+Shift+Y when a check is focused), `checks.rerunSuite` (Ctrl+Alt+Y), `palette.navigate.up/down` (arrow keys inside palette), `palette.confirm` (Enter), `palette.dismiss` (Escape). Add 'Open settings' (Ctrl+,), 'Toggle theme' (no shortcut), 'Compose comment' (the `composer.open` above), 'Mark file viewed' (the `file.markViewed` above), and a 'Switch composer posting identity' command that opens the existing M4 posting-identity quick-switch.
      * Dynamic: each saved reply gets an auto-registered command `savedReply.insert.{id}` with title `Insert: {name}` and the run-function calls the composer's insert API.

   b) **Palette UI** — `apps/desktop/src/lib/components/palette/CommandPalette.svelte`:
      * Primer-styled modal (uses Primer's `Dialog` + `ActionList` patterns). Opens via `Ctrl+K` (or `Cmd+K` on macOS).
      * Layout: search input on top + filtered command list below, grouped by `section`. Each row shows title + section badge + shortcut (right-aligned, Primer Kbd).
      * Search: case-insensitive fuzzy match over `title + keywords` (use a tiny fuzzy library or hand-roll a simple Smith-Waterman / subsequence match — measure both and pick the faster one).
      * **Perf budget**: open in < 75 ms (mount + initial render). Result list in < 150 ms (filtered render). To hit these, the palette is preloaded as a hidden component the first time it's opened — subsequent opens are cheap. The command list is virtualized via `@tanstack/svelte-virtual` (already a dep from the diff viewer) when > 50 results. Each search keystroke debounced to 16 ms (one frame) and the filter runs in a RequestIdleCallback when supported.
      * Sticky 'Recently used' section at the top (last 5 commands the user invoked, persisted in localStorage keyed by `palette.recent`). Saved-reply commands count.

   c) **Keyboard layer** — `apps/desktop/src/lib/commands/keymap.ts`:
      * A single source-of-truth keymap declared statically; each entry maps a shortcut to a command id.
      * Mounted globally at `apps/desktop/src/routes/+layout.svelte` via a `<svelte:window on:keydown={handle}>`-style listener; resolves context (activeRoute / activePrId / focused-element type) at keydown time, then dispatches the matched command through the registry.
      * Respects input focus: when a `<textarea>` / `<input>` is focused, non-modifier-key shortcuts (e.g. plain `r`, `c`) are SUPPRESSED to avoid hijacking typing. Modifier-bearing shortcuts (Ctrl+K, Ctrl+Shift+R) still work.
      * Sequence shortcuts (`g i`, `g p`, `g s`) use a small state machine with a 500 ms timeout after the lead key.
      * Documented in a new `apps/desktop/src/routes/settings/keyboard/+page.svelte` Keyboard tab showing every shortcut grouped by section.

   d) **Account-switch command** — `account.switch` opens a small inline palette listing all accounts; arrow keys + Enter switches the active account. This is a leaner spawn-on-top palette rather than a separate UI — share the palette component.

   e) **'Open in github.com' commands** — `pr.openInGithub` calls `tauri-plugin-shell::open(pr.html_url)` (via existing Tauri shell plugin if installed; otherwise add it). `inbox.openInGithub` opens the active account's inbox URL (`https://github.com/issues?q=author:@me` or notifications page; pick the one matching github.com's keyboard shortcut + document).

   f) **Perf bench** — add a new `tools/perf-bench/command-palette.mjs` script measuring:
      * **Open time**: time from `Ctrl+K` keystroke to the palette being rendered + focused. Measure via the existing perf-bench harness (the one used by `pnpm bench`). Budget: < 75 ms.
      * **Result time**: time from typing a query to the filtered results rendering. Budget: < 150 ms.
      Both measurements are min-of-N per the m1-fix-gates policy. Surface in `tools/perf-bench/run-all.mjs` so `pnpm bench` runs them and gates on the budgets.

2) **Backend (Rust)** — minimal: just the `tauri-plugin-shell` integration for the 'Open in github.com' commands (if not already present). No new mutations.

3) **Playwright spec** `apps/desktop/playwright/m5-command-palette.spec.ts`:
   * Open palette: `Ctrl+K` → assert modal opens + focus is in the search input. Measure the open duration via `page.evaluate(performance.now)` deltas; assert < 75 ms.
   * Filtered results: type `open inbox` → assert the matching command appears + result render < 150 ms.
   * Run command: Enter → assert navigation to the inbox.
   * Sequence shortcuts: press `g`, then `i` → assert navigation to inbox. Press `g`, wait 600 ms, press `i` → assert nothing happens (timeout).
   * Input-focus suppression: focus the composer textarea, press `r` → assert nothing happens (no command invoked).
   * Apply suggestion via palette: open palette on a PR with suggestions, search 'apply suggestion', Enter → assert the SuggestionBatchModal (from m5-suggestion-apply) opens.
   * Resolve thread via palette: open palette on a PR with a focused thread, search 'resolve thread', Enter → assert the resolve mutation fires.
   * Mark file viewed via palette: open palette in the diff viewer with a file focused, search 'mark file viewed', Enter → assert the IPC fires.
   * Open in github.com via palette: search 'open in github', Enter → assert `tauri-plugin-shell::open` is called with the PR's html_url.
   * Saved reply via palette: search 'Insert', pick a saved reply, Enter → assert the composer textarea has the saved-reply body inserted.
   * Recently-used section: invoke 'open inbox' twice → reopen palette → assert 'open inbox' appears in the 'Recently used' sticky section.
   * Keyboard-only PR cycle: starting from the inbox, navigate to a PR with `g p` + number, focus a thread with `j`/`k` (if defined; else add them), resolve it with `Ctrl+Shift+R`, mark the file viewed with `v`, open in github with `Ctrl+Shift+O` — all WITHOUT touching the mouse. Record a Playwright video to `artifacts/m5-keyboard-layer/full-cycle.webm` (or numbered screenshots).
   * Screenshots to `artifacts/m5-command-palette/`.

4) **Accessibility audit** — add a Playwright test under the existing `a11y-pr-detail.spec.ts` (or a new `m5-a11y.spec.ts`) running axe-core against: the inbox, a PR detail, the composer with saved-replies open, the command palette open, the SuggestionBatchModal open, the rerun-checks rail. Assert no critical violations.

5) **DECISIONS.md** — dated M5 entry covering: (a) the command registry design (static + dynamic merge); (b) the keyboard layer's input-focus suppression policy; (c) the sequence-shortcut state machine + timeout choice; (d) the palette virtualization threshold + preload strategy (how we hit the < 75 ms / < 150 ms budgets); (e) the recently-used persistence shape; (f) which 'Open in github.com' URL each command points at.

### Guardrails
